text:
linda: Heads-up — ran a quick `npm audit` after the latest `pnpm install` in console/ui. Output shows 1 critical + 2 high. Need triage and a patch prioritization plan.

raj: Can you paste the vuln IDs and which packages are affected? direct vs transitive?

linda: Critical is CVE-2025-xxxx -> package `mem` <=4.0.1 pulled in transitively via `css-loader` -> `postcss` chain. Highs are `minimist` (prototype pollution) and `serialize-javascript` (XSS-ish in older versions). Quick excerpt:

```
# npm audit quick
# Critical: 1  High: 2
mem 4.0.1 - prototype poll. -> via css-loader@5.2.0 > postcss > ...
minimist 0.0.8 - prototype poll. -> minimist@0.0.8 (transitive)
serialize-javascript 2.1.0 - insecure eval -> serialize-javascript@2.1.0
```

linda: `npm ls mem` shows: console-ui -> css-loader@5.2.0 -> postcss -> mem@4.0.1

taylor: Ugh. css-loader is a build-time plugin but we bundle parts of it into the prod bundle via our webpack config (we inline css for critical styles). So this is in the final artifact — treat as production-impacting.

kevin: Agreed. Proposed priority: Critical -> 24h SLA, High -> 72h. Plan: try to upgrade css-loader to a version that pulls mem patched; if that forces big lockfile churn, consider a targeted resolution/override for mem only and a small follow-up to upgrade css-loader properly.

raj: We're on pnpm. We can add a `pnpm.overrides` entry to force `mem@^4.0.2` (patched) which only updates transitive dep without sweeping everything. That reduces churn and risk.

linda: I can open a quick PR with the override and run the console-e2e and bundle size CI. Branch: `security/mem-override-1954`.

sec-bot: CVE-2025-xxxx: mem 4.x prototype pollution. CVSS 9.1. Public PoC available. Affects server and some client bundles depending on usage.

taylor: Also: check our SBOM and SCA results; add regression tests to ensure css loader path doesn't reintroduce mem usage. If override works, we should still schedule a follow-up to upgrade css-loader and adjust loaders to avoid bundling unnecessary parts.

kevin: For `minimist` and `serialize-javascript` — quick check: minimist appears in some devtools CLI packages; serialize-js is a runtime dep in older html sanitizer lib we vendor. We'll triage on the same PR or separate? I prefer separate PRs to keep rollouts small.

raj: Separate PRs is safer. Set priorities: mem (critical) -> immediate override PR + hotfix release; minimist (high) -> patch in 72h if it's reachable in prod; serialize-js -> patch and add unit tests for sanitizer output, target next minor.

linda: I'll open the mem override PR and link the audit output + CI runs. tagging @taylor for bundle review and @kevin for release cut. I'll also include a short rollback plan: revert override and cut hotfix if bundle regression.

taylor: Sounds good. Also please add a note in the release changelog and notify product/security channels once the hotfix is live. :thumbsup:

kevin: After hotfix, we should schedule a short follow-up sync to discuss long-term solution (move away from bundling css-loader runtime, or switch to safer loader config). 30-min meeting tomorrow?

linda: Meeting invited. I'll post PR link here when created.

sec-bot: Created advisory ticket SEC-2025-78 and assigned to eng-security.

linda: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/4200 — includes `pnpm.overrides` forcing `mem@4.0.4`, CI passing locally. Please review quick.
